id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

subjectType.description: The Type that mixes {@link MlSubject} and that represents the modelled ML subject.

router.description:
Router to use to dispatch predictions requests to the correct models.
A router cannot be used by more than one project.

If not specified at the creation of the project, an instance of {@link MlModel.RelationRouter} is created
by default.

subjectFilter.description:
Filter to select the subjects in scope for this project (it is applied to the {@link subjectType} type).
If null, all the subjects are in scope for the project.

All the filters used in the project (e.g. when deploying a model or defining a segment) will be restricted with
this filter (with an "and" clause).

Note that this field must be set when the project is created. It cannot be modified later.

@see MlDeployment#subjectFilter
@see MlSubject.Group#resolvedSubjectFilter

targetTypes.description:
Target types that the model outputs can be transformed to for downstream consumption (e.g. persistence).
{@link MlModel.OutputHandler Output handlers} that perform the transformations will make best-effort validation
of the target types, see {@link MlModel.OutputHandler#validate}.

interpretTargetTypes.description:
Target types that the model interpretation outputs can be transformed to for downstream consumption (e.g. persistence).
{@link MlModel.OutputHandler Output handlers} that perform the transformations will make best-effort validation
of the interpret target types, see {@link MlModel.OutputHandler#validate}.

healthValues.description:
Total order of possible health values (i.e. enumeration) for a {@link MlModel} in this project. The order should
be from "best" status (e.g. "GREEN", "P3", "HEALTHY") to "worst" status (e.g. "RED", "P0", "UNHEALTHY").
If not specified, then the default order will be lexicographical.

Here are some possible examples:
["GREEN", "YELLOW", "RED"]
["P3", "P2", "P1", "P0"]
["HEALTHY", "UNHEALTHY"]

See {@link MlModel.Health.Value#health}.

title:
A `MlProject` represents a Data Science use case and regroups all the artifacts related to that use case,
such as ML {@link MlModel models}, {@link MlSubject subjects}, {@link MlDeployment deployments} or
{@link MlSubject.Group segments} (groups of subjects), among others.

The key field is {@link #subjectType}: it defines the Type of the modelled ML subject.

Example:
```type
entity type WindTurbine mixes MlSubject
```
```py
project = c3.MlProject(
    id="Predictive Maintenance",
    subjectType=c3.WindTurbine
).merge()
name: MlProject
